parts.title: Part 1 · Sounds Quick Drill

parts.title: Part 2 · Teach & Review Concepts for Reading

Use explicit Letter-Sound Tile builds to repair exact reading of three-letter blends and up to six sounds.

data.conceptNotes: Accuracy repair: read every grapheme in a three-letter blend. Each consonant in the blend keeps its own sound. Maintain exact endings and cumulative welded-sound accuracy.

parts.title: Part 5 · Sentence Reading
teacherDirections: Have the student read each selected sentence silently and then aloud, one at a time.
Use the paired weave question after the sentence while preserving accurate reading, phrasing, and meaning.

sentences: Grab some string so we can bind the two boxes.
I will also fix the straps.
There will be buds on each and every branch in the spring.
The world has a very strong crust.
Do not tempt me to go for a swim.
Not one word about this script!
I had to scrap my plan at work.
I was struck by how very old and drab that quilt was.
Everyone thinks Sal is too strict.
Would Chad want to work on the script for us too?
weaveQuestions: What three letters form the beginning blend in string?
Read strap-straps. What beginning letters do you actually see?
Find the word with a three-letter blend. Name the letters in the blend.
What three letters begin strong? Keep the whole blend intact as you read.
Read the sentence with phrasing that makes the meaning clear. What does tempt mean here?
In scrap, how is /k/ spelled when it follows the three-letter blend?
What three letters begin struck? Do not add or replace a sound.
Compare script with strong: what beginning blend does each word actually show?

parts.title: Part 6 · Quick Drill in Reverse
teacherDirections: Dictate each selected previously taught phoneme and require the student to repeat the sound and name the corresponding grapheme(s).

parts.title: Part 7 · Teach & Review Concepts for Spelling
teacherDirections: Begin with the four selected previous-substep words.
For current 2.5 words, require every sound in the three-letter blend before spelling.
Reinforce that /k/ in the targeted three-letter scr- blend words is spelled c.

data.conceptNotes: Accuracy spelling repair: represent every consonant sound in the three-letter blend; in the targeted scr- words, spell /k/ with c.
troubleSpotTargets: Eleanor: say the actual initial blend before spelling.
Nora: hold the exact ending before committing to the word.
Levi: keep welded-sound review cumulative and brief.

parts.title: Part 8 · Written Work Dictation
teacherDirections: Require the student to repeat each dictation item before spelling.
Proofread phrases and sentences and mark selected current/cumulative concepts.

sentences: I think that I can split the logs.
Chad will jump with a big splash.
Fran still has to scrub the pots.

data.markReinforce: Mark the three-letter blend; reinforce c for /k/ in scr- words; keep cumulative welded-sound markings accurate.

parts.title: Part 9 · Controlled Text Passage Reading
teacherDirections: Read the selected controlled passage, reread for phrasing/repair, and answer the ten documented comprehension questions.
Passage history remains explicitly uncertain rather than inferred.

data.passage:
Clint is not glad about the gust of hot wind. Spring is coming! Most everyone in the world feels bliss when the sun lasts long into dusk. Yet, Clint could not help but think of all the work. When all the cold and frost ends, the land and grass would be a mess.

Each spring Clint has to trim the shrubs and fix up the mulch bed. Spring has sprung, so his tasks are at hand. Black mold masks the shed. Clint finds sticks and globs of rank sod everywhere. Clint is very strong, but this is too much stress and filth!

In his mind, Clint tempts himself with a snack and a nap, but he must go on. He scrubs the swing and the two benches by the elm. Then he sets two pots on the front steps. He plants the bulbs one by one, then splashes them with water.

When everything is fresh, Clint grasps that he should not be such a grump. He lugs the trash out back and sprints to have a bath and grill some lunch.

questions.question: What season is coming in the passage?
Name two jobs Clint has to do outside.
What does Clint want to do instead of continuing the work?
Why does the warm spring weather make Clint think about work instead of only feeling happy?
What does ‘grasps’ mean near the end of the passage?
How does Clint change the yard as he works?
Why does Clint decide he should not be such a grump?
What can you infer about Clint’s character from the fact that he keeps working even when he wants a snack and a nap?
What details show that the job felt difficult at first but became worthwhile?
What message does the passage give about attitude and finishing an unpleasant job?
